title: Fibre components occur in closures of generic-fibre components
statement: Let $S$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point], and let $f:X\to S$ be a flat morphism of schemes [def-weil-flat-morphism]. For $s\in S$ and an irreducible component $C$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] of the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], there exists a generic point $x\in X_s$ of $C$. For every such $x$, there exist an irreducible component $B$ of $X_\eta$ and its generic point $z\in X_\eta$ such that, regarding $x,z$ as points of $X$ via the fibre inclusions, $x\in\overline{\{z\}}$. Moreover $C$, identified with its image in $f^{-1}(s)$, is an irreducible component of the subspace $\overline{\{z\}}\cap f^{-1}(s)$ of $X$. No local finite type, Noetherian, density, or equidimensionality hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0GSK (remark-flat-equidimensional), second list: reduction to closures of generic-fibre components; affine lifting uses Algebra Tag 00HS (lemma-flat-going-down), algebra.tex.

proof.text: Write $i_t:X_t\to X$ for the fibre inclusion. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre] this identifies $|X_t|$ homeomorphically with $f^{-1}(t)$. The component $C$ is closed and irreducible by [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Apply [lem-sc-scheme-sober] to the scheme $X_s$: it has a generic point $x$ with $C=\overline{\{x\}}^{X_s}$. Fix any such $x$, so the remainder applies to every generic point required in the statement.

Since $\eta$ is generic in $S$, $s\in\overline{\{\eta\}}$ by [def-sc-generic-point]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-generalizations-lift] to $f$, $i_s(x)$ and $\eta$: flatness supplies $y\in X$ with $f(y)=\eta$ and $i_s(x)\in\overline{\{y\}}$. Here “$v$ specializing to $f(t)$” in that node means $f(t)\in\overline{\{v\}}$. Use the fibre homeomorphism [def-pc-scheme-fibre] to regard $y$ as a point $y_\eta\in X_\eta$.

source.place: Tag 03HV (lemma-generalizations-lift-flat), the scheme form of Algebra Tag 00HS (lemma-flat-going-down); Schemes Tag 01K1.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], choose an irreducible component $B$ of $X_\eta$ containing $y_\eta$. By [lem-sc-scheme-sober], choose its generic point $z$, so $y_\eta\in\overline{\{z\}}^{X_\eta}$. Under the embedding [def-pc-scheme-fibre], this says $y\in\overline{\{i_\eta(z)\}}^X\cap f^{-1}(\eta)$. Put $Z=\overline{\{i_\eta(z)\}}^X$. As $Z$ is closed and contains $y$, it contains $\overline{\{y\}}^X$, hence $i_s(x)\in Z$.

source.place: Tag 004W (lemma-irreducible), part (4); Schemes Tags 01IS and 01K1; assembly for More on Morphisms Tag 0GSK (remark-flat-equidimensional), second list.

proof.text: The subspace $Z\cap f^{-1}(s)$ is closed in $f^{-1}(s)$ and contains $i_s(x)$. The fibre homeomorphism [def-pc-scheme-fibre] therefore shows that it contains $i_s(C)$, the closure of $i_s(x)$ in that fibre. The set $i_s(C)$ remains irreducible in this intermediate subspace: its induced topology is unchanged. If an irreducible subset $D$ of $Z\cap f^{-1}(s)$ contains $i_s(C)$, its topology as a subset of $f^{-1}(s)$ is also unchanged, so it is irreducible there. Maximality of $C$ in $X_s$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] forces $D=i_s(C)$. Thus $i_s(C)$ is an irreducible component of $Z\cap f^{-1}(s)$, as asserted.
